item.title: Oklahoma agrees to share private voter data with DOJ in settlement
item.description: State Attorney General Gentner Drummond announced on Tuesday that a settlement has been reached in the lawsuit filed by the U.S. Department of Justice against the Secretary of the State Election Board for access to Oklahoma's private voter information.

item.title: Classen drive closes in Midtown; New development under construction
item.description: Construction has started in Midtown on a new project, and you may have noticed that Classen Drive is now closed. That will be a permanent closure to make way for The Eddie, a new development now under construction.

item.title: Alan Armstrong focused on energy infrastructure in new Senate role
item.description: Oklahoma Governor Kevin Stitt has appointed energy executive Alan Armstrong to the U.S. Senate, replacing Markwayne Mullin.

item.title: Woman helps mothers with babies in NICU after loss of her son to rare disease
item.description: On September 21, 2023, the family made their way to the hospital to welcome baby Jack. It turned into a day that changed the family's life forever.

item.title: KFOR Investigation reveals former Fairview City Manager accused of embezzlement
item.description: KFOR is investigating an allegation of embezzlement against the former city manager of Fairview, Oklahoma involving an expensive piece of ground-clearing equipment.

item.title: Courtroom battle ends with attorney in handcuffs
item.description: A hearing ends in Pontotoc County with an Oklahoma attorney led out in handcuffs.

item.title: OKC metro police chase involving stolen car ends with fiery crash, 2 suspects on the run
item.description: Moore police officers say a Friday morning chase with the driver of a stolen car ended in a fiery southeast metro crash that damaged several vehicles at a car dealership.

item.title: Three arrested in Grady County high-speed chase
item.description: Grady County deputies were involved in a chase near Dibble, Oklahoma, on Friday afternoon.

item.title: OKC Police officers suspended while 'April Fools' prank is investigated
item.description: Oklahoma City Police say officers involved in an 'April Fools' prank are now on administrative leave.

item.title: TSET staff leaving as lawmakers look at dissolving it
item.description: Thursday, the Executive Director of the Tobacco Settlement Endowment Trust announced her resignation. This, as House lawmakers push for a possible dissolution of TSET.

item.title: Federal jury awards $126 million to family of teen killed in crash with former Moore police officer
item.description: A federal jury has decided that the city of Moore, along with a former Moore police officer, will pay $126 million for a car accident that tragically killed a teenager in 2019.

item.title: Tinker Elementary Earns Purple Star Status for Supporting Military Families
item.description: It was an exciting end to the school week at Tinker Elementary. The school was designated as a Purple Star School, which is a huge honor for the district.
